summary: Compare perpendicular pressure samples with a value-space magnetic-field derivative of parallel pressure, reporting pointwise and aggregate residuals.

identity.relation: Parallel pressure and magnetic-field samples to an expected perpendicular pressure and residual
identity.direction: (p_parallel, p_perp, B) -> rhs, error, relative_error, aggregate errors, passed
identity.definition: Sort flattened samples by B, estimate d[p_parallel/max(B, 1e-30)]/dB with a first-order-edge finite gradient, and map the derivative back to input positions. Set rhs=-B^2 times that derivative, error=p_perp-rhs, and relative_error=abs(error)/max(abs(p_perp),abs(rhs),atol) elementwise; passed means max(relative_error)<=rtol.
identity.model: Saved Pleiades value-space parallel-pressure consistency relation, not a spatial force-balance residual
identity.geometry: No spatial geometry is used; array dimensions are preserved only as sample layout
identity.coordinates: Derivative coordinate is magnetic-field value B after flattening and sorting, not R, Z, arc length or array index
identity.boundary: With one sample or magnetic-field range at most 1e-30, derivative is defined as zero. A nondegenerate field range requires sorted B samples separated by more than 1e-30.
assumptions: For a physically interpretable p_parallel/B relation, the caller supplies a meaningful positive magnetic-field magnitude, although the callable only checks finiteness.
The finite-difference result depends on the supplied B-value sampling, including endpoint spacing.

inputs.name: p_parallel
inputs.shape: nonempty scalar or array; exactly the same shape as p_perp and magnetic_field
inputs.constraints: All values finite; negative values are not rejected.

inputs.name: p_perp
inputs.description: Perpendicular pressure samples compared with the derived right-hand side.
inputs.shape: exactly the same shape as p_parallel
inputs.constraints: All values finite; negative values are not rejected.

inputs.name: magnetic_field
inputs.description: Magnetic-field values used as the global value-space derivative coordinate.
inputs.shape: exactly the same shape as p_parallel
inputs.constraints: All values finite; the implementation does not require positivity. A nondegenerate sample set may not contain duplicate or near-duplicate B values within 1e-30.

inputs.name: rtol
inputs.description: Maximum allowed normalized residual for the passed flag.

inputs.name: atol
inputs.description: Absolute pressure scale flooring the normalized-residual denominator.

inputs.name: strict
inputs.description: When truthy, raise if the maximum normalized residual exceeds rtol.
inputs.constraints: Interpreted by Python truth value; the implementation does not enforce bool type.

outputs.name: rhs
outputs.description: Value-space estimate of -B^2 d(p_parallel/B)/dB, with a 1e-30 denominator floor on B.
outputs.constraints: Finite on successful return; zero derivative when B has no resolved spread.

outputs.name: relative_error
outputs.constraints: Finite and non-negative on successful return.

outputs.name: max_relative_error
outputs.description: Maximum of all pointwise relative errors.

outputs.name: mean_relative_error
outputs.description: Mean of all pointwise relative errors.

outputs.name: passed
outputs.description: Whether max_relative_error is at most rtol.
outputs.constraints: No result is returned on failure when strict is truthy.

preconditions: Pressure arrays and magnetic-field values describe the same nonempty sample set and share an exact shape.
The caller has selected a physically meaningful magnetic-field coordinate and sampling for this value-space pressure relation.
supported: Scalar or array-shaped finite sample sets with a resolved, nonduplicate B-value range.
Degenerate all-equal B samples under the explicit zero-derivative convention; non-strict reporting or strict rejection of tolerance failure.
excluded: A spatial derivative or local MHD force-balance test on a grid.
Physical interpretation of negative or near-zero B values without an independently justified convention.
Finite-difference convergence or equilibrium validity beyond the supplied sample set.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for mismatched shape, empty samples, nonfinite values, invalid rtol/atol, or duplicate B values in a nondegenerate sorted sample set. Conversion failures may propagate from NumPy.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if rhs or residual outputs become nonfinite; with truthy strict, also raises ValueError when max_relative_error exceeds rtol.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; the derivative is a finite sample gradient, not an iterative solve.
failure_semantics.partial_results: None; strict failure and invalid inputs return no result mapping.

provenance.lineage_summary: SciRel maintains the parallel-pressure residual relation from saved Pleiades development-migration material. That historical candidate record is not an expert approval or a currently qualified D1 source freeze; the exact source qualification and scientific interpretation remain review questions.
source_kinds: saved Pleiades operator descriptor and migration provenance
SciRel direct value-space and failure-behavior regression tests

example.description: Check the value-space relation on unsorted magnetic-field samples.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.diagnostics import compute_parallel_pressure_residual
B = np.array([3.0, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0])
r = compute_parallel_pressure_residual(B * B, -B * B, B, rtol=1e-12)
np.testing.assert_allclose(r['rhs'], -B * B, rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12)
assert r['passed'] and r['max_relative_error'] <= 1e-12
example.expected: Sorting by B recovers rhs=-B^2 in the original sample order; the supplied p_perp passes the selected residual threshold.

scope: Constant p_parallel/B and zero perpendicular-pressure identity.
Unsorted B-value example, all-equal B zero-derivative convention, strict-mode tolerance rejection and empty-input failure.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Direct tests establish the listed algebraic and finite-sample behavior only. They do not compare a current qualified source oracle, establish a spatial derivative, prove physical equilibrium on an arbitrary geometry, or constitute expert scientific approval.
known_limitations: All array positions are pooled into one B-sorted derivative; spatial adjacency is discarded.
The B denominator is floored at 1e-30 and nonpositive B is not rejected, so callers must restrict physically meaningful usage themselves.
Degenerate B sampling forces a zero derivative regardless of pressure variation.
Public distribution licensing and expert recognition remain pending.
